rationale.conceptual: The method is a standard application of classical molecular dynamics with an off-the-shelf force field. Only minor variations (supercell construction, composite model compression) are needed, and all analysis metrics are textbook post-processing of MD trajectories.
rationale.execution: The reproduction requires a multi-stage pipeline: building four models from crystal structures, setting up and running 20 NPT simulations, and then computing several different quantities (bond lengths, CED, binding energy, elastic constants). The orchestration involves handling file I/O, simulation log parsing, and combining results; it is neither trivial nor overly complex.

difficulty.reasoning: The paper employs classical MD with the well-known COMPASS force field and standard NPT ensemble; no novel algorithm or custom derivation is required. The pipeline involves building crystal models, running 20 simulations (4 systems × 5 temperatures), and post-processing bond lengths, cohesive energies, and elastic moduli – a multi-stage but standard orchestration.

compute_estimate.reasoning: The simulations involve small systems (2400 atoms) with a classical force field; they can run comfortably on a single CPU core with less than 1 GB of RAM, and the input data (crystal structures, force field parameters) is negligible.
